payload.feature:
Decision 0041 (docs/decisions/0041-one-office-per-seat.md) is accepted; rulings 1 to 7 have landed. This slice enacts ruling 8 exactly as written — a charter is three texts, and the engine renders two of them — with its enforcement binding. Read the decision first; it is the commission. Decision 0042 (docs/decisions/0042-the-council-is-brokkrs-the-dialect-is-the-realms.md), also accepted, shares the contract this slice opens and is named below where it matters.

The office. Every library charter in agents/charters/ names no repository: no toolchain command, no path of this repository, no decision number of this repository, no bundle name. What a charter says is the office — what the seat does, what it must not do, its result vocabulary — and nothing about the house it works in. Move every repository-specific sentence the charters carry today (the Rust-only rule, the frozen contracts and the read-only production table, `cargo test --workspace`, the self-bundle compile, the decision-document convention, the commit style, "never push") into one house file for this realm, `docs/house-rules.md`, written as the rules of the house a seat reads before it works.

The house rules are the realm's. `forge.realms/v3` (contracts/realms.v3.schema.json, beside v1 and v2, frozen-contracts test and contracts/README.md table updated) adds two optional fields per realm: `house`, a repository-relative path to a Markdown file, and `dialect`, the name of a spec dialect or a repository-relative path — decision 0042 ruling 1 opens `dialect` and this slice only declares it, so the loader accepts it, pins it in the manifest beside the realms pin and does nothing else with it until 0042's own slice; a v2 map keeps loading exactly as it did. When the realm names a `house`, the engine renders its content into every seat prompt under a `## House rules` heading, after the charter and before the run context, and pins the file's digest into the run manifest beside the realms pin (a manifest version bump only if the existing shape cannot hold it additively; say which). `realms.json` in this repository names `docs/house-rules.md`. A realm that names none renders nothing, and a charter that needs a house rule it cannot find is a defect of the realm, which `brokkr doctor` reports.

The result contract is the engine's. The prompt assembly in crates/brokkr-protocol/src/adapters.rs renders the result contract from the site's own vocabulary: a non-final sequence step sees its own results, the final step and every single seat see the seat's. Delete the paragraph in agents/charters/chief-architect.md, position-simplicity.md and position-robustness.md that disclaims "the generic result contract below", and any charter sentence that restates a vocabulary the engine now renders. A test drives a sequence through the fake driver and asserts a non-final step's prompt carries its own vocabulary and not the seat's, and that the final step's carries the seat's.

The roster test walks agents/charters/ for the repository tokens it lists — `cargo`, `crates/`, `bundles/self`, `decision 00`, `policy/`, `fixtures/`, `contracts/` — and refuses them, its comment naming the reading (a charter is an office; the house is the realm's). The recipes' own role files (recipes/*/roles/) are not library charters and keep whatever their recipe needs; recipes/node's roles may now adopt the library agents wherever they differed from them only by house rules, with a sample house file for a Node repository under docs/guides/starters/ and docs/guides/adopting-a-node-repo.md pointing at it; where a Node role differs in office (its verify script), it stays a role and the roster test's exception list says so. The guides — agent-library.md, recipe-authoring.md, repository-layout.md, driver-authoring.md — describe the three texts and where each lives.

Tests. Realms v3 loads a v2 map unchanged and a v3 map with both fields; the house digest lands in the manifest and a changed house file moves the run's identity; the engine renders the heading exactly once per seat prompt and nothing when the realm names none; the prompt-vocabulary test above; the roster token walk; every witness and compose digest that moves is re-pinned with the reason in the test's own words.

Constraints: the exact coverage gate (scripts/coverage-exact.sh, run with stdin closed: </dev/null) must stay at literal 100%; clippy -D warnings and fmt must stay clean; cargo test --workspace green; contracts/, fixtures/ and policy/phase-machine.json are read-only — v3 lands beside v1 and v2 and existing contract files are not edited; the decision index docs/decisions/README.md must keep every row main carries in number order; do not name the private neighbours in prose; keep the CLI list "claude, codex or dsh" whenever a list of harnesses appears; commit in the repository's style and never push.


Two rules learned on an earlier fire, stated up front: every test that compares a path the product reports or prints against a path the test built compares them as `Path`s or after canonicalizing both sides — never as strings with a separator inside a component — because macOS's temp directory is a symlink and Windows paths carry a verbatim prefix and backslashes; and paths inside a hands box are POSIX strings joined with `/` whatever the host. The CI test job runs with `--no-fail-fast`, so a platform reports every failing binary at once.

A third rule, learned on the select fire: a guide or README that this slice touches is updated, never gutted — every reference section it carries today stays, revised for what changed, and the index lines that point at it stay true; deleting a section is a finding, not a simplification.

result.notes: Enacted Decision 0041 ruling 8: portable charters, realm-owned house and dialect declarations with manifest pins and doctor enforcement, engine-rendered house and site result contracts, v3/v8 contracts, guides, and regression coverage. Workspace tests, fmt, clippy -D warnings, and exact coverage are green; committed without pushing.

cargo test --workspace: 58 successful test-suite summaries, 0 failed; cargo run -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/self: 1 bundle compiled, 0 failed (offline from the bound Cargo registry cache)

Reviewed d37413b (decision 0041 ruling 8) for correctness, simplicity and security; changed nothing. fmt clean, clippy -D warnings clean, cargo test --workspace green (58 suites). The exact coverage gate could not be launched from this seat (command refused); it rests on the implementer's reported 100% and is not re-verified here. Security: none above info. House text is confined to the realm by is_repository_relative (loader and schema both refuse absolute, drive-letter and '..' spellings), is pinned with a content digest the rehydrate path re-derives, and is rendered with the same trust a charter already has; the pin carries the host-absolute source path exactly as the realms pin does. Findings that remain: [MEDIUM, correctness/simplicity] crates/brokkr-runtime/src/bundle.rs parse_sequence: a 'results' key on a sequence step that also carries an 'aggregate' is accepted and silently ignored — Aggregate::required_results() wins, a mismatching array is never refused, and the key is now in STEP_KEYS on every step. recipes/triage/bundle.json carries the decorative key on three panel steps (moving the triage and night-shift witnesses for data the compiler discards) and docs/guides/recipe-authoring.md teaches it, stating that the array on every non-final step is that step's vocabulary, which is false for panel steps. Either refuse 'results' beside 'aggregate' or refuse a mismatch, and correct the guide and bundle. [LOW, correctness] engine.rs ~1504: a non-final Single step's declared vocabulary is prompt-only; an off-vocabulary result is stored into prior_results with no check (decide() validates only the seat's final result). Not a regression, but the manifest now pins a vocabulary the engine does not enforce. [LOW, simplicity] tests/roster.rs tool_grants_are_invoked_by_the_library: a library agent's tool grant is now justified by this realm's docs/house-rules.md (cargo for implementer, implementer-speckit, implementer-engine); a library invariant is proved by realm data, and in another realm those grants have no text behind them. [LOW, test-coverage] engine/tests.rs a_sequence_fake_driver_sees_step_results_then_the_seat_results hand-writes seq_input.steps[].allowed_results rather than deriving it through seat_input, so the derivation at engine.rs:707/733 is proved only indirectly, and it asserts the driver input, not the rendered prompt (the render is covered separately in adapters/tests.rs). [LOW, docs] docs/guides/repository-layout.md: the contracts/ row lost its enumerated versions and decision citations (0022, 0023, 0026) and the realms.json row lost decision 0023 — condensed rather than revised, against the rule that a touched guide is never gutted. [LOW, correctness] doctor.rs report_realm_house labels every World::discover error (malformed map, unknown schema) as a MISSING 'house rules' line. [LOW, robustness] realms.rs World::pin indexes self.texts[&realm.name], which panics on a world rehydrated by from_manifest whose pin lacks 'realm' over a multi-realm map; unreachable from today's single caller. [LOW, charters] intake.md/intake-speckit.md dropped the guidance to read README.md and docs/decisions/ 0004 and 0005 without moving it into docs/house-rules.md. Not findings: recipes/node roles were not adopted onto library agents, which the framing permits ('may') and the Node implementer differs in office (no intake phase) not only house; contracts/ untouched except the two new files and the README table; decision index unchanged; no new harness list in prose.

Reforged ruling 8 after review: aggregate step vocabularies are validated, all intermediate results are enforced before entering context, prompt coverage derives through the engine, realm and doctor error paths are robust, and condensed house/guide text is restored. Formatting, clippy -D warnings, cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast, and exact 100% line/branch/function coverage all pass; committed as 8d119b0.

Reviewed d37413b and 8d119b0 against 881c4e4 for correctness, simplicity and security. Verified here: cargo fmt --check clean, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings clean; verify reported cargo test --workspace green and bundles/self compiling; the exact coverage gate cannot be run from this seat's sandbox, so 100% is unverified by me. Findings, most severe first. (1) MEDIUM correctness/contract — contracts/run-manifest.v8.schema.json requires `results` on every sequence step (definitions.step.required), but body_manifest in crates/brokkr-runtime/src/bundle.rs:1147 still emits only {name, body}; no engine manifest satisfies v8, while every one still satisfies v7. contracts/README.md (lines 38-42), the compose_tests UNCOMPOSED comment, the witness_digests comment and docs/guides/recipe-authoring.md all claim per-step vocabularies are pinned in the manifest; they are only pinned through the bundle file's digest. Either emit `results` in the manifest (and re-pin) or withdraw v8 and the prose, since the framing allowed a bump only when v7 could not hold it additively. (2) MEDIUM correctness, many-hearth regression — load_realm_texts in crates/brokkr-runtime/src/realms.rs reads the house of EVERY realm at World::load, so a v3 map naming a house for a neighbour realm whose tree is not checked out on this machine refuses the whole world: run, runs, tui, watch and doctor all fail for an unrelated realm. This contradicts the module's own rule that the map is evidence about intent, not a mount check (absolute(), test a_realm_whose_tree_is_not_there_yet_still_compares), and is unnecessary because pin() only carries the selected realm's texts. Read lazily for the selected realm, or tolerate an unreadable house on unselected realms and let doctor report it. (3) LOW correctness — parse_sequence (bundle.rs ~2110) accepts a `results` array on the FINAL step via STEP_KEYS and silently overrides it with the seat's vocabulary; an author's declared final vocabulary is ignored without refusal. (4) LOW security — brokkr-core is_repository_relative rejects `/`, `\`, `C:/`, `C:\` and `..`, but admits the Windows drive-relative form `C:foo`; on Windows Path::join treats the `C:` prefix as a new root, so a house or dialect can resolve outside the realm root. The map is operator-authored, hence low; the v3 schema regex has the same gap. (5) LOW simplicity/docs — recipes/node/roles/implementer.md keeps the full Node house prose that docs/guides/starters/node-house-rules.md now duplicates, so an adopter following adopting-a-node-repo.md gets the same rules twice in each prompt; and the index lines still say 'the four files your repo needs' (docs/guides/README.md:20, docs/guides/quickstart.md:414) while the guide now says five, against the rule that index lines pointing at a touched guide stay true. (6) LOW test-coverage/doctor — house_rules propagation into panel members and sequence steps (engine.rs 1229, 1462, 1524) is executed but asserted nowhere (only seat_input is tested); report_realm_house discovers the map from the process cwd with no map name, so `brokkr doctor` ignores a `--realms` the other surfaces honour. No injection, journal-tamper or fail-open path found: the house pin is content-hashed and re-derived on resume, prompt rendering only adds a heading before the task block, the non-final vocabulary check fails the effect closed. Charters carry no listed repository token; guides updated not gutted; decision index untouched; harness lists unchanged.

Resolved the returned review: v8 manifests now emit and validate effective step vocabularies, final-step overrides are refused, unreadable neighbour houses no longer break a world while selected houses fail closed, doctor honours --realms, drive-relative realm text paths are rejected, Node house prose is single-sourced, and panel/sequence propagation is asserted. Formatting, clippy -D warnings, cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast, self-bundle compile, and exact 100% line/branch/function coverage pass; committed as d7cc5b4.

cargo test --workspace: 58 successful test-suite summaries, 0 failed; cargo run -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/self: 1 bundle compiled, 0 failed (offline from the bound Cargo registry cache)

Reviewed d37413b, 8d119b0 and d7cc5b4 against 881c4e4 (decision 0041 ruling 8) for correctness, simplicity and security; changed nothing. Verified here: cargo fmt --check clean; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings clean; `brokkr recipes list` compiles all eight recipes and both system bundles under the new per-step results rule; the verify seat reported cargo test --workspace green (58 suites). The exact coverage gate cannot be launched from this seat (command needs an approval the sandbox refuses); the implementer's three result files report literal 100% and that is not re-verified by me. Both earlier review rounds' medium findings are answered in the reforge commits: body_manifest emits `results` and every witness manifest validates against run-manifest/v8; neighbour houses are read lazily per realm and only the selected realm's failure refuses; the final-step `results` key is refused; drive-relative spellings are refused in loader and schema; doctor honours --realms and labels a broken map as the map; a non-final result outside its vocabulary fails the effect closed before it becomes prior context; the v8 bump is justified in contracts/README.md and the schema description (v7 closes the step shape). Resume rehydrates the house from the manifest pin, so an edited house cannot change a resumed run's prompts. Findings that remain, none above low: [LOW, docs] docs/guides/cards/node.md:44 still says recipes/node's charters name `npm ci` and `npx tsc --noEmit` explicitly; after this slice recipes/node/roles/implementer.md names neither (only roles/verify-seat.sh and the adopter's house do), so a card pointing at a touched recipe is now untrue. [LOW, simplicity] recipes/node/roles/implementer.md is now the library implementer charter minus one sentence (no intake phase); the framing permitted adopting the library agent, and a near-verbatim role copy will drift from agents/charters/implementer.md. [LOW, correctness] two quiet paths render no house for a realm that declares one: Cmd::Run accepts no --repo, and a run started without a repository over a v3 map pins no `realm`/`house` and renders nothing without a diagnostic; and realms.rs pinned_texts over a multi-realm map whose pin lacks `realm` drops a carried `house` pin instead of refusing. [INFO, simplicity] engine.rs 1229/1462/1524 hand members and steps `"house_rules": null` when the seat input omits the key; brokkr-core realms.rs `#[inline(never)]` on is_repository_relative and the runtime's `allow(clippy::manual_map)` are coverage-gate accommodations unique in the tree, the first without a comment saying so; the dialect pin repeats the declared string as source, hashed bytes and content. [INFO, security] house text is rendered verbatim into every seat prompt with a charter's trust and pinned at run start; confinement is by spelling (absolute, drive-letter and `..` refused) not by canonical path, so a symlinked house can read outside the realm and its content is then pinned into the journal; it is operator-authored repository data of the same class as recipe roles, and no seat can alter a later prompt inside its own run. No injection through seat results or driver output, no journal tamper path (the house pin re-derives its digest on rehydrate like the map pin), no protocol confusion (driver-protocol input is an open object), no secrets touched, no fail-open path. Charters carry no listed repository token; guides updated not gutted; decision index untouched; no new harness list in prose.
